text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Abilene ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Abilene Profile Boots History Identification Sources brand introduced 1980; company formed 2002 · Somerset, Pennsylvania Abilene began in 1980 as the western-boot division of the B.B. Walker Company, and in 2002 a group of its managers bought the division and set it up as Abilene Boot Company. The boots are made in Somerset, Pennsylvania, in a factory the company says has made footwear since the 1940s. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with Abilene, Texas. History Abilene is a Pennsylvania boot brand, not a Texas one. The company’s own history, which Boot Barn reprints, says the Abilene label was introduced in 1980 as the western division of the B.B. Walker Company. In 2002 a team of the company’s managers bought the Abilene division and set it up as Abilene Boot Company, which it says is still entirely privately held by its members. B.B. Walker was a North Carolina footwear maker. Its founder built a shoe factory in Asheboro in 1947, and production there ended in 2001. Somerset County property records list Abilene Boot Co., Inc. as the owner of a parcel on South Center Avenue in Somerset that it got from the B B Walker Company. The company is at 841 South Center Avenue in Somerset, Pennsylvania. title: Acme Boots | Western Boot World
text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Acme Boots ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Acme Boots Profile Boots History Identification Sources 1935–mid-1980s peak · Clarksville / Ashland City, Tennessee From the 1940s into the mid-1980s, Acme was a high-volume Tennessee cowboy-boot factory. Depression-era Acme Shoe Manufacturing in Clarksville pivoted to cowboy boots in 1935. Later the name moved through Arena Brands, a 2000 Texas Boot Company license, and 2002 sale to H.H. Brown under the Double-H family — so a post-~2000 Acme mark is not evidence of Clarksville/Ashland City golden-age production. Related: Double-H Boots · Dingo Why collectors care Acme floods the secondary market. An Encyclopedia that covers Justin , Nocona , Lucchese , Tony Lama , and Dan Post but skips Acme leaves a daily ID hole. Value is scale and survival , not artisan scarcity — teach dating and ownership, do not romanticize factory boots as custom. Golden rule: an Acme mark from the licensing / Double-H era is not proof of Clarksville / Ashland City golden-age production. Company history Treat round “pairs per day / headcount” blog figures as approximate unless tied to contemporary trade reporting. Exact production figures need contemporary documentation. title: Lucchese | Western Boot World
text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Lucchese ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Lucchese Profile Boots History Identification Sources founded San Antonio 1883; El Paso from 1986 · San Antonio → El Paso, Texas Lucchese was founded in San Antonio in 1883 by Sicilian immigrants Salvatore “Sam” Lucchese and his brother Joseph as Lucchese Bros. Boots & Shoes, a shop near Fort Sam Houston. Early customers included cavalry officers. Cosimo Lucchese took daily management after Sam's 1923 stroke and incorporated Lucchese Boot Company after Sam's death in 1929. Samuel J. Lucchese became president after Cosimo's death in 1960. The company was sold to Blue Bell, parent of Wrangler, around 1970, ending day-to-day family ownership; sources differ on the exact sale year. Headquarters and production moved from San Antonio to El Paso in 1986. Arena Brands, formerly Hat Brands, acquired the company in 1998, and the firm adopted the Lucchese Bootmaker name in 2012. The official timeline later names a 2023 Chris Stapleton collaboration and a 2024 Dallas Cowboys official-boot partnership. Related: Sam Lucchese Company history Lucchese Boot Company is the manufacturing house that grew from the 1883 San Antonio shop opened by Sicilian immigrants Salvatore “Sam” Lucchese and his brother Joseph near Fort Sam Houston. text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Tony Lama ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Tony Lama Profile Boots History Identification Sources c. 1911–13 · El Paso, Texas An Italian-immigrant cobbler who started repairing soldiers' boots at Fort Bliss and built the most recognized western boot brand in the world. In the 1950s he pushed exotic skins and bold styling into the mainstream, the exotics era starts here. Related: Tony Lama Signature Series · Tony Lama Sr. · Larry Mahan Why collectors care Tony Lama is both a person and the El Paso production house that made exotics mainstream. Founder biography now lives on Tony Lama Sr. . This page keeps company stamps, plants, and later Justin Brands ownership, plus the distinction from the Tony Lama Signature Series line page. Sources differ on the founding year: the brand uses 1911 , TSHA gives 1912 , and a 1962 El Paso Times account gives 1913 . The approximate range 1911–13 reflects that disagreement. Tony Lama Sr.: life and career Italian immigrant parents; orphaned about age 11 ; shoemaker apprentice. Fort Bliss cobbler (~ 1910 , Sixth Infantry / Pershing context per TSHA). Opens the El Paso shop; marries Esther Hernández 1917 ; six children in the company. Dies January 1974 ; succession Tony Jr. / Bert (Joseph). Company history c. 1911–13: Repair shop + about 20 pairs in year one. By 1933: about 40 pairs/day (TSHA). title: Dan Post | Western Boot World
text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Dan Post ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Dan Post Profile Boots History Identification Sources est. 1965 · Tennessee Brought cushioned comfort and exotic skins to production price points, the boots that let a working paycheck own ostrich. Related: Dingo Why collectors care Dan Post sits in the Encyclopedia shelf rail next to Justin , Nocona , Lucchese , Ariat , Tecovas , Cuadra , and Sendra . On the secondary market it is one of the most common exotic-at-working-price labels — ostrich, caiman, lizard, snake, shark, and related skins — so identification questions are frequent. Useful questions: What era is this pair? Who owned the name? Where was it built? How do I separate Dan Post from Laredo and Dingo, and from handmade El Paso customs? Brand origin Company materials date the brand to 1965 / the mid-1960s and emphasize “Handcrafted Cushion Comfort.” Dan Post is a brand identity , not a documented master-bootmaker biography. McRae Industries / Dan Post official materials and contemporary trade reporting are stronger than colorful founder stories on secondary blogs. Texas Monthly (June 2002) notes that Lloyd Easterling , later running L.M. Easterling Custom Boot Company in Fredericksburg with boots built in El Paso, was a former Lucchese and Dan Post president . title: Frye | Western Boot World
text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Frye ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Boot Manufacturer Frye Profile Boots History Identification Sources est. 1863 · Marlborough, Massachusetts; later made in other U.S. plants, Mexico and China John Addison Frye opened a small shoe shop in Marlborough, Massachusetts, in 1863, and the company says its first boot followed in 1888. Frye’s first cowboy boot, the Rancher, came in the 1940s, and its strap-and-ring Harness boot became a 1960s and 1970s icon alongside the Campus boot. The family sold the business in 1949, and it has changed hands many times since. History The Frye Company began in Marlborough, Massachusetts. The company dates its start to March 1863, when John Addison Frye opened a small shop on Elm Street. A company history in the International Directory of Company Histories says Frye, the son of a Marlborough shoe manufacturer, learned the trade at the S.H. Howe Shoe Company, started with a partner who each put in $150, and bought the partner out within a year. He began with modestly priced women’s and children’s shoes, then added boys’ shoes and men’s nailed and pegged shoes and boots. By 1865 the business had moved to a larger building, which he enlarged half a dozen times. Sources give his birth year as 1839 or 1840. His son Walter Preston Frye joined in 1887, and the company says it made its first boot in 1888. title: Charlie Dunn | Western Boot World
text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Charlie Dunn ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Bootmaker Charlie Dunn Profile Boots History Identification Sources 1898 to 1993 · Austin, Texas Charles Russell Dunn was born on 19 September 1898 on the White River in Arkansas and became Austin’s best-known custom bootmaker through Lone Star Shoe Service, a long back-room tenure at Capitol Saddlery, and Texas Traditions from 1977. Jerry Jeff Walker’s 1972 song made his name a cultural marker, not construction proof. Lee Miller bought the shop in 1986 and continues the method at Texas Traditions. Dunn died on 23 September 1993. Related: Texas Traditions · Lee Miller Why collectors care Charlie Dunn is the cultural and craft ancestor of Texas Traditions . Collectors meet his name through Jerry Jeff Walker’s 1972 song, celebrity client lists, and Austin oral history, then need a sober way to evaluate claimed pairs. Value rides on authorship, provenance, and shop era, not model numbers. The song is a cultural marker, not construction proof. He was born on 19 September 1898 and died on 23 September 1993 . Lee Miller bought Texas Traditions in 1986 . Biography Charles Russell Dunn was born on 19 September 1898 on a houseboat on the White River in Arkansas. Gene Fowler’s Illume Connect essay of 1 January 2020 places the family at Glory, near Paris, Texas, after a covered-wagon move when Charlie was three. text_excerpt: Home / Boot Encyclopedia / Earl Beck ← Manufacturers & Bootmakers Bootmaker Earl Beck Overview Biography Identification Sources est. 1916 (Dalhart); moved to Amarillo 1921 · Dalhart, Texas; later Amarillo, Texas Earl Beck, with his twin brother Bearl, bought a boot shop in Dalhart, Texas, in 1916 and moved the business to Amarillo in 1921, founding what became Beck Boots. His son, Harry Beck, later ran and eventually sold the Amarillo shop. Known for Co-founder of Beck Boots with twin brother Bearl Related: Beck Boots · Bearl Beck Biography History Earl Beck was one of twin brothers who bought a boot shop in Dalhart, Texas, in 1916 and moved it to Amarillo in 1921, founding what became Beck Boots . His twin brother was Bearl Beck , who worked alongside him. Earl's son Harry Beck later ran the business and eventually sold it. No birth or death year for Earl has surfaced.
